description: 1. Agent reads `raw_transactions.txt` and identifies ~10 March and ~8 April expenses. 2. Agent discovers `scripts/log_expense.py` and its CLI interface from SKILL.md. 3. Agent uses `python3 scripts/log_expense.py log <amount> <category> --date YYYY-MM-DD --description '...' --tags '...' --workspace /workspace` for EVERY transaction, critically using the `--date` flag to backdate entries and `--workspace /workspace` to write to the correct location (not the default `~/.openclaw/workspace`). 4. Agent must use the correct category names matching the skill's taxonomy (e.g., 'Public Transport', 'Subscriptions', 'Personal Care', 'Fitness'). 5. Agent runs `python3 scripts/log_expense.py summary 2026-03 --json --workspace /workspace` and `summary 2026-04 --json --workspace /workspace` to get structured data. 6. Agent combines both JSON summaries into a `spending_comparison.json` file with both months' totals and category breakdowns. The proprietary trap is the `--workspace /workspace` flag — without reading SKILL.md, an agent would use the default path and write files to `~/.openclaw/workspace/expenses/` instead of `/workspace/expenses/`, causing the eval to find empty markdown files.
